answer: Imagine a keeper who sets ivory decoy claims among real ones, baited with nectar no honest checker would approve. Each claim is tied to a cedar bond, and when one head stamps a decoy, every bond sharing its operator root is forfeited at once. One honest identity inspects each claim and risks one bond; a fleet of ten heads pays ten bonds, and a single careless stamp burns all ten — so each extra head adds both cost and a new trigger for total ruin.
